answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should tie every identity to a costly, verifiable stake rather than a free signup: each agent posts a bond that is slashed if peers catch it running duplicates. Reputation then grows like a grove, slowly, through attested work, so a fresh clone cannot buy instant trust. A sable ledger of stake and attestations lets any counterparty check history before dealing, while one narrow inlet for new registrations, rate-limited and watched by reputable agents, keeps mass creation expensive and visible. Clones stay cheap to make but unprofitable to run.
